correctness.rationale: Exact theorem over all connected simple graphs, proved through a finite-dimensional Rayleigh-order lemma, centered quadratic-form projection, degree-sum graph classification, and explicit regular/star affine laws; special complete graph handled separately. Four-path rational witness values (-2/9,13/12) and (-4/9,11/12) have equal sums 8 and squared norms 22. Checker independently evaluates all 27475 connected labeled graphs at orders 2..6; this is a cross-check, not the proof of all orders. Extension to equal mean and variance uses centered unit vectors and common translation.

evidence: de Jong, Sprenger & van Veen (1984), full paper, considers independent extremal eigenvalues of two centered forms, not ordering all pairs simultaneously.

Bavaud (2024), sections on weight-compatible reversible weights, gives proportional Moran/Geary in a balanced weighted model; uniform-weight raw adjacency of an irregular star does not meet that model's balancing condition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The published balanced-weight simplification does not dominate a classification for unbalanced raw adjacency; extremal values for each statistic alone do not imply universal ordering between every pair of signals. A broader unknown algebraic characterization remains possible.

originality.rationale: Inspected full texts cover the spectral extremal framework (1984), the existing degree-weighted algebraic Moran-Geary identity (2017), and balanced normalized weights (2024). None of those inspected results states or implies the full graph-theoretic iff characterization for rank comparison of all real-valued attributes under uniform-weight raw adjacency, including the exceptional nonregular star, nor the first order-four reversal. Regular-graph formulas are treated as prior, not claimed as new; the theorem distinguishes its all-real input domain from restricted-alphabet special cases. Unread plausible coverage is disclosed.

Cross-comparisons with pre-existing binary-profile analyses do not establish global publication priority.

value.rationale: The problem is motivated by real disagreements in ranking social/spatial node attributes using two classical autocorrelation metrics. The theorem gives a natural all-orders iff network-topology characterization, an unexpected nonregular star exception, and the sharp smallest equal-mean equal-variance counterexample on four nodes. These are substantive structural and minimality results, not only recomputations or the already published degree-weighted identity; they may guide interpretation where the same network carries multiple continuous attributes. No empirical statistical inference or application guarantee is claimed.
